title: Labelled motion-component taxonomy
description: Versioned, machine-applied labels over stored numeric evidence. Every label is a predicate over named fields, not a creative archetype. Layer D is specified but has no stored evidence in this corpus.

layers.name: Pacing and timing
layers.description: Cut-candidate rate, shot-gap statistics, per-third pace trend, and strobe/burst texture. Rate labels are bands; trend and texture labels are orthogonal to the bands.

layers.name: Temporal appearance
layers.description: Second-to-second luma instability, static-pair share, and least-squares luma drift with an R-squared requirement. Derived from the stored 1 Hz appearance series.

layers.name: Audio energy
layers.description: Integrated loudness bands, loudness range, onset density, tail silence, and loudness slope with an R-squared requirement. Only assigned where an audio record is joined.

layers.name: Transition and global motion
layers.description: Transition-vocabulary shares, global translation fractions, centre-weighted local motion, and overlay-activity proxy. Specified against the real motion_profile fields; no record in this corpus carries the block, so no label can be assigned today.

layers.name: Editorial-behaviour composites
layers.description: Small conjunctions of measured pace, appearance and audio components. A composite is refused when any component is missing, even if the remaining components point the same way.

layers.name: Explicitly out of scope
layers.description: Names that this taxonomy deliberately does not assign. They are listed so that consumers cannot mistake an adjacent numeric label for a claim about style, effect identity, genre, quality, intent or authorship.

labels.label: single-shot
labels.definition: The full-runtime scan found no scene-score exceedance, so the record has one interval between start and end.
labels.reuseNote: Use as the zero-detected-event end of the cut-rate scale; do not read it as an unbroken take in the editorial sense.
nonClaims: Does not prove the work has a single shot: an undetected cut, a locked-off long take and a continuous generated image all produce the same scan.
Does not establish camera movement, subject continuity or editorial intent.

labels.label: long-take
labels.definition: Detected scene-change rate is below the long-take ceiling and at least one scene candidate exists.
labels.reuseNote: Use for low detected-event density; pair with a separate text search if a specific take length matters.
nonClaims: A low detected-event rate is not a verified take length: missed cuts shorten apparent shots and false candidates split them.
Does not establish that the camera holds, that the action is continuous, or that the shot is the editorial unit.

labels.label: steady-cut
labels.definition: Detected scene-change rate falls in the middle band between the long-take ceiling and the rapid-montage floor.
labels.reuseNote: Default middle-band label for corpus aggregation; do not treat it as a style or genre class.
nonClaims: Describes a candidate-event rate over the runtime, not a rhythmic pattern, beat alignment or editing philosophy.
Does not distinguish hard cuts from fades, dissolves, flashes or false candidates.

labels.label: rapid-montage
labels.definition: Detected scene-change rate is at or above the rapid-montage floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use as the high-density end of the cut-rate scale; cite the rate and the candidate-event caveat together.
nonClaims: Fast movement, flashes, strobe and compression can inflate the candidate count, so a high rate is not proof of rapid editing.
Does not establish shot count, transition type, pace change within the runtime or editorial intent.

labels.label: accelerating
labels.definition: The stored per-third pace ratio is above the accelerating band, and the derived trend names acceleration.
labels.reuseNote: Use only as a direction-of-change signal between first and last thirds; keep the ratio alongside it.
nonClaims: Third-to-third ratios are sensitive to where the cuts happen to fall and to false candidates.
Does not show a smooth ramp, a musical build, or a deliberate escalation.

labels.label: decelerating
labels.definition: The stored per-third pace ratio is below the decelerating band, and the derived trend names deceleration.
labels.reuseNote: Use only as a direction-of-change signal between first and last thirds; keep the ratio alongside it.
nonClaims: Third-to-third ratios are sensitive to where the cuts happen to fall and to false candidates.
Does not show a fade-out, a slow ending, or a deliberate release of tension.

labels.label: strobe-texture
labels.definition: The census strobe flag is true, meaning the sampled luma series exceeded the stored instability threshold.
labels.reuseNote: Use as a photic-texture caution signal; it is a sampled instability flag, not an edit or a safety verdict.
nonClaims: Not an editing label: strobe texture can come from flashing content inside a shot, from a strobe light, or from compression artefacts.
Not a photic-safety measurement: the 1 Hz appearance series aliases higher frequencies and cannot certify a flash rate.

labels.label: burst-texture
labels.definition: At least half of the detected cut gaps are shorter than the stored burst-gap ceiling.
labels.reuseNote: Use to separate clustered candidate events from evenly spread ones at the same average rate.
nonClaims: A burst of candidate events is not a verified rapid sequence; it can be motion or luminance artefacts.
Does not establish a montage, a chase, a stinger or any narrative function.

labels.label: flicker-high
labels.definition: Median absolute second-to-second luma change is at or above the high-instability floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use as a sampled instability band; quote the 1 Hz cadence with it.
nonClaims: Not a flicker frequency or a flash-rate measurement; the 1 Hz series aliases content above roughly 1 Hz.
Does not identify strobing, flashing, lightning, camera shake or an effect.

labels.label: flicker-low
labels.definition: Median absolute second-to-second luma change is at or below the low-instability ceiling.
labels.reuseNote: Use as the low end of the sampled instability scale, not as a stillness claim.
nonClaims: A low sampled instability value does not mean the image is still, nor that the shot is locked off.
Cadence aliases fast variation, so low values can coexist with visible flicker.

labels.label: static-frame-dominant
labels.definition: The static-pair share of consecutive appearance samples is at or above one half.
labels.reuseNote: Use to flag records whose sampled appearance changes little between consecutive seconds.
nonClaims: A static appearance pair is not a static camera or a still frame; slow motion and long dissolves can also change little per second.
Does not establish a freeze, a title card or a held composition.

labels.label: luma-rise
labels.definition: The least-squares luma slope is positive at or above the drift floor, with an R-squared at or above the drift-fit floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use only with the reported R-squared; the slope alone is dominated by single bright passages.
nonClaims: A fitted upward drift is not a creative brightening, a reveal, or a deliberate tonal arc.
R-squared is fit quality over 1 Hz samples, not evidence of causation or continuity.

labels.label: luma-fall
labels.definition: The least-squares luma slope is negative at or below the negated drift floor, with an R-squared at or above the drift-fit floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use only with the reported R-squared; the slope alone is dominated by single dark passages.
nonClaims: A fitted downward drift is not a fade, a blackout, or a deliberate tonal arc.
R-squared is fit quality over 1 Hz samples, not evidence of causation or continuity.

labels.label: loud-mix
labels.definition: Integrated loudness is above the gate and at or above the loud band floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use as a band on measured integrated loudness; never as a mix-quality judgement.
nonClaims: A loud integrated level is not loudness compliance, clarity, impact or a quality verdict.
The value is a programme-loudness measurement of one mixed stream; it says nothing about dialogue, music or effects separately.

labels.label: quiet-mix
labels.definition: Integrated loudness is above the gate and at or below the quiet band ceiling.
labels.reuseNote: Use as the low band of measured integrated loudness; keep the gate note with it.
nonClaims: A quiet integrated level is not intimacy, restraint, a mix defect or a quality verdict.
Records at or below the -70 LUFS gate are reported as at-or-below-gate and receive no loudness band.

labels.label: wide-lra
labels.definition: Measured loudness range is at or above the wide-range floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use to separate records with a broad measured level range from compressed ones.
nonClaims: Loudness range is a statistical spread of short-term loudness, not a dynamic-style, genre or quality judgement.
Does not localise the loud and quiet passages, and does not establish a build or a drop.

labels.label: narrow-lra
labels.definition: Measured loudness range is at or below the narrow-range ceiling.
labels.reuseNote: Use to flag a compressed measured level range; pair it with the actual LRA value.
nonClaims: A narrow range is not a loudness-war verdict, a format convention or a quality judgement.
Does not show that the record is dynamically flat to a listener or that the mix is consistent in intent.

labels.label: onset-dense
labels.definition: Detected envelope onsets per minute of runtime are at or above the dense floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use as an amplitude-envelope event-density band, not as a beat or edit-sync indicator.
nonClaims: Onsets are amplitude-envelope rises, not musical beats, cuts, hits or speech events.
Dense onset detection can come from percussive music, speech, noise or effects; no source separation is performed.

labels.label: onset-sparse
labels.definition: Detected envelope onsets per minute of runtime are at or below the sparse ceiling.
labels.reuseNote: Use as the low end of the envelope-event density scale.
nonClaims: Sparse onsets are not silence, a drone, an ambient score, or a deliberate restraint.
The detector is causal and threshold-based; sustained sounds with smooth attacks can yield few onsets.

labels.label: silent-tail
labels.definition: Measured tail silence is at or above the silent-tail floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use to detect trailing silence in the measured stream, for example when trimming or concatenating.
nonClaims: Tail silence may be an artefact of the rendition, the encode, or the source's own end card, not an editorial choice.
Does not establish an ending, a button, a fade-out or a pause in the narrative.

labels.label: loudness-rise
labels.definition: The least-squares loudness slope is positive at or above the loudness-drift floor, with an R-squared at or above the loudness-fit floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use only with the reported R-squared; a positive slope over a long record is easily produced by one loud section.
nonClaims: A fitted loudness rise is not a build, a crescendo, a drop or a deliberate energy arc.
R-squared is fit quality across the runtime, not evidence of causation or listener-perceived change.

labels.label: loudness-fall
labels.definition: The least-squares loudness slope is negative at or below the negated loudness-drift floor, with an R-squared at or above the loudness-fit floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use only with the reported R-squared; a negative slope over a long record is easily produced by one quiet section.
nonClaims: A fitted loudness fall is not a release, a fade, a breakdown or a deliberate energy arc.
R-squared is fit quality across the runtime, not evidence of causation or listener-perceived change.

labels.label: hard-cut-dominant
labels.definition: At least the stated share of detected scene candidates is classified as hard-cut by the fixed transition vocabulary.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; the share is a proxy from short windows, never transition ground truth.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, the transition classes are fixed proxies that can confuse flashes, fast motion and compression with edits.

labels.label: dissolve-using
labels.definition: The combined short-dissolve and long-dissolve shares reach the stated dissolve share floor.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; the class is a graded-change window proxy.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, short and long dissolve classes do not establish a specific transition effect, direction or intent.

labels.label: fade-using
labels.definition: The combined fade-through-black and fade-through-white shares reach the stated fade share floor.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; fade detection is a recovered luma extreme, not an editorial fade.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a recovered luma dip or peak does not establish a fade to black or white as an edit.

labels.label: pan-dominant
labels.definition: At least the stated share of observable frame pairs has global image-plane displacement at or above the pan threshold.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; pan is an image-plane translation hypothesis, not a camera move.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a pan fraction cannot separate camera, subject and post moves, and parallax or zooms violate the translation model.

labels.label: static-camera
labels.definition: At least the stated share of observable frame pairs is at or below the static displacement threshold.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; the label is about image-plane stillness, not a rig or a tripod.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a majority of static translation pairs does not establish a static camera, a locked-off rig, or an absence of internal subject motion.

labels.label: centre-weighted-motion
labels.definition: The centre cell's share of measured frame-to-frame RGB change is at or above the stated centre-share floor.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; the 3x3 distribution describes where change is measured, not what is framed.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, a centre-heavy change distribution is not a subject position, a composition or a compositional intent.

labels.label: overlay-active
labels.definition: The larger of the upper-third and lower-third high-frequency luma volatility proxies is at or above the overlay-activity floor.
labels.reuseNote: Do not assign until a motion-profile re-scan exists; this is a volatility proxy, not text, logo or graphic detection.
nonClaims: Cannot be assigned from the current corpus: no census record contains motionProfile.
Even when measured, high-frequency luma volatility does not identify text, a logo, a lower-third, a title or any graphic element.

labels.label: front-loaded
labels.definition: The pace trend decelerates, the last-to-first third ratio is at or below the front-load ceiling, and the first third is at or above the early-rate floor.
labels.reuseNote: Use when both the direction and the magnitude of the early density are present; never on the trend alone.
nonClaims: Front-loaded does not mean a hook, a cold open, a trailer structure or an audience-retention tactic.
The composite is a conjunction of measured rate ratios, not an editorial reading of the opening.

labels.label: building
labels.definition: Pace accelerates while either fitted luma or fitted loudness rises above its floor, with every component measured.
labels.reuseNote: Use as a strict three-component conjunction; if audio is missing the composite is refused rather than inferred from picture alone.
nonClaims: Building does not mean a narrative build, a musical crescendo, a rising action or an intended climax.
The label is a conjunction of a pace ratio and one fitted appearance or loudness slope; each component retains its own caveats.

labels.label: flat-steady
labels.definition: The pace trend is steady and the fitted luma drift stays inside the flat band with a low R-squared.
labels.reuseNote: Use as a no-trend conjunction for baseline or control records; it is not a calm or neutral style label.
nonClaims: Flat-steady does not mean calm, restrained, contemplative or monotonous.
A flat appearance fit and a steady pace ratio can coexist with strong internal motion, colour change or loud audio events.

labels.label: animation-style
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not name an animation technique, medium or production method.

never.reason: no stored field measures animation technique or medium

labels.reuseNote: Do not derive style from pacing, appearance or motion proxies; use a separately labelled, human-coded study if needed.
nonClaims: Does not identify stop-motion, CG, cel, collage, mixed media, hand-drawn or any other technique.
Would require labelled frames or a trained, validated classifier with documented error rates.

labels.label: vfx-effect-identity
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not identify a visual effect, filter, grain, glow, distortion, particle or compositing operation.

never.reason: no stored field measures effect identity

labels.reuseNote: Do not infer effects from luma volatility, edge density or motion proxies; those are not effect detectors.
nonClaims: Does not identify blur, glow, grain, distortion, particles, keying or any compositing operation.
Would require an effect-labelled dataset and a validated detector, plus a stated confusion matrix.

labels.label: transition-ground-truth
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not assert a verified edit type, cut frame or transition boundary.

never.reason: scene-score candidates and transition windows are proxies, not verified edits

labels.reuseNote: Do not use layer D or layer A counts as ground-truth edit lists; they are candidate events and fixed-vocabulary proxies.
nonClaims: Does not establish that a cut occurred at a frame, that a dissolve lasted a stated time, or that a fade reached black.
Would require frame-accurate human annotation with an inter-annotator agreement statistic.

labels.label: video-template-detection
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not match a record against a template, format, package or campaign system.

never.reason: no stored field measures template or package membership

labels.reuseNote: Do not cluster records into templates from these labels; use an explicit template library and matching method.
nonClaims: Does not identify a reusable package, a design system, a template family or a campaign system.
Would require a template library plus a matcher with a measured false-positive rate.

labels.label: camera-rig-inference
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not infer a camera body, lens, rig, gimbal, drone or physical move.

never.reason: no stored field measures camera or rig identity

labels.reuseNote: Do not read the layer D pan or static proxies as camera facts; they are image-plane translation summaries.
nonClaims: Does not establish a dolly, crane, handheld, gimbal, drone or locked-off camera.
Would require EXIF/rig metadata or a validated camera-motion model with calibrated ambiguity handling.

labels.label: genre
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not classify genre, format, market or audience category.
labels.reuseNote: Use catalog metadata if genre is needed; do not infer it from motion labels.
nonClaims: Does not identify music video, commercial, title sequence, brand film, trailer or any other genre.
Would require a labelled genre corpus or the catalog's own editorial categories, used as a separate field.

labels.label: quality
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy makes no quality, craft, taste or award-worthy judgement.
labels.reuseNote: Do not rank or filter on these labels as if they encoded quality; use them as descriptive strata only.
nonClaims: Does not rank records, measure craft, predict awards or establish audience response.
Would require a defined rubric, trained raters and an inter-rater reliability statistic.

labels.label: intent
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not infer creative intent, brief, strategy or narrative purpose.
labels.reuseNote: Do not translate measured behaviour into a purpose statement; keep the measurement and the interpretation separate.
nonClaims: Does not establish why a choice was made, what a client asked for, or what a sequence is meant to achieve.
Would require creator interviews, briefs or a labelled intent study with documented coding rules.

labels.label: authorship
labels.definition: Not assigned: the taxonomy does not attribute a work to a person, studio, tool or model.
labels.reuseNote: Use catalog credits for attribution; never infer authorship from measured behaviour.
nonClaims: Does not identify a director, studio, animator, tool or generative model.
Would require provenance metadata or a validated authorship-attribution method with a stated error rate.
